summary: CRM customer-engagement domain foundation adds account registration metadata, opportunity qualification metadata, quote preparation metadata, service-case opening metadata, marketing-campaign planning metadata, loyalty activity recording metadata, and SAP CRM/CX parity-map linkage while explicitly refusing durable customer master persistence, CDP unification, CPQ pricing, order-management mutation, service routing, marketing journey execution, message delivery, loyalty wallet settlement, Workflow execution, cloud deployment, and runtime audit-chain claims.

findings: The slice is additive and isolates CRM customer-engagement invariants in a flat microservice crate rather than widening Enterprise Suite into a CRM monolith.
The API remains pure data-in/data-out with no I/O, durable state, network clients, CPQ runtime, service routing, marketing delivery, loyalty settlement, or execution-side mutations.

claims_allowed: ERP parity-map linkage for SAP CRM/CX
findings: Independent scaling and deployment remain future adapter/runtime work; this slice only creates the pure domain foundation.

F3_adversarial.diagnostic_asserted: Tests fail if missing account registration, missing opportunity qualification, unsafe refs, credential-shaped evidence refs, invalid dates, invalid lifecycle scores, zero amounts, invalid probabilities, discount guardrail violations, invalid campaign refs, or zero loyalty points are accepted.
findings: Positive account-to-opportunity-to-quote-to-service-case-to-campaign-to-loyalty flow and negative guard rails are covered.
Types map directly to customer accounts, opportunities, quotes, service cases, marketing campaigns, and loyalty activities common to CRM/CX systems.

alternatives_named: leave CRM as a parity gap
add CRM customer-engagement domain foundation first
F6_alternatives.selected_rationale: A flat domain foundation gives CRM parity a service-owned first write path while keeping durable customer master, CDP unification, CPQ, order management, service routing, marketing journey execution, message delivery, loyalty settlement, Workflow, and cloud adapters out of scope.
rejected_reasons: Leaving CRM as a gap weakens ERP parity after SCM/APO, PM, QM, PP, warehouse, procurement, and treasury foundations landed.
Live CRM/CX runtime requires durable customer/profile stores, CPQ/order/service/marketing/loyalty integrations, operational SLOs, and cloud evidence beyond this slice.

findings: No credentials, external network calls, customer-profile fetches, order mutations, message delivery, service routing, loyalty settlement, or Workflow dispatches are introduced.
Policy, source, and audit refs reject traversal, whitespace/control, and credential-shaped strings.

F8_performance.regression_baseline: Pure string/date/quantity validation and bounded arithmetic only; no I/O or unbounded data access exists.

findings.summary: No database, network, filesystem, CPQ engine, journey runtime, delivery channel, loyalty wallet, or hot runtime path is introduced.

data_class_touched: FINANCIAL lifecycle scores, revenue, probability, quote, discount, budget, points, and monetary values
findings: SAP, Oracle, and Microsoft official materials inform CRM/CX coverage only; no exhaustive vendor parity or proprietary behavior clone is claimed.
The change is additive: one new crate/spec/catalog row and parity-map references; no migration or external resource is introduced.
Static evidence, task rows, and audit-chain rows document the change; runtime audit emission remains a non-claim.
No production user or data migration exists.
Package name follows oya-crm-customer-engagement-domain and flat microservice layout.
Machine-readable CRM spec and existing task ledger capture the slice without creating root markdown sprawl.
The new domain crate depends only on oya-data-boundary-kernel and adds no third-party dependencies.
